newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan central bank cuts repo rate to 19 pct.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan central bank cuts repo rate to 19 pct.

text.p: The State (central) Bank of Pakistan (SBP) on Wednesday slashed its key three-day repo (repurchase contract) rate, or discount rate, to 19 percent from 20 percent a year.

"It has been decided to reduce the SBP 3-day repo rate against short-term federal bonds and federal investment bonds by one percent to 19 percent per annum with effect from 18th June, 1997," an SBP circular said.

The SBP repo rate, last changed on October 22, determines the interest charged by the central bank on amounts provided as temporary funding facility to commercial banks that fail to sqaure their positions in the overnight inter-bank money market.

"The financing facilities to be provided by the State Bank for meeting temporary liquidity shortage shall, with immediate effect, be remunerated by the recipients at a minimum rate of 19 percent on annual basis," the circular said.

No central bank official was immediately available for comment, but bankers said the move was in line with government policy of bringing down the overall interest rate structure to enable the corporate sector to borrow at lower rates.
